proposal.utterance: Classify 'an act of promising' in BFO terms.

entities.label: ActOfPromising
entities.rationale: An act of promising is a temporally extended happening — a speech act or communicative event — performed by an agent. It unfolds in time (it has a beginning, middle, and end), and is thus a Process (BFO_0000015). It is not a continuant because it does not persist through time maintaining identity; rather it occurs. It is a kind (common noun), so it is a class, not an individual.

relations.rationale: ActOfPromising is a subclass of Process (BFO_0000015) because it is a temporally unfolding occurrent.

open_questions: Should ActOfPromising be further refined as a subclass of a more specific process type already in the ontology (e.g., BehavioralLegalManifestation) if the promise is legally significant, or should it remain a direct subclass of BFO Process?

Is the intent to model 'an act of promising' purely as a social/communicative process, or specifically as a legally operative act (e.g., a contractual offer or acceptance)? If the latter, it may also bear a Role or Disposition (e.g., a ContractualOffer role realized in the promising process).
Should the promisor (bearer of an obligation-generating role) be modeled as a participant in this process via RO_0000057 (has participant)?
proposal.rationale_summary: An act of promising is paradigmatically an occurrent: it happens, it unfolds in time, and it cannot be said to persist through time the way a person or a document does. BFO 2020 places such happenings under Process (BFO_0000015). The promise is a kind of communicative or speech-act process in which at least one agent (the promisor) participates. The content of the promise — what is promised — is a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031), and any obligation generated by the promise would be a specifically dependent continuant (a Role or Disposition, BFO_0000023/BFO_0000016) inhering in the promisor. Since the utterance asks only for the classification of 'an act of promising' and uses a common noun, it is best represented as a class, not an individual. No existing working class directly captures this concept, so a new class ActOfPromising is proposed as a subclass of BFO_0000015.
